limits.limit: (a) Toasts and body-level tips outside an open native modal are inert.
limits.plain_meaning: This limit applies only to a modal you opt into with `native: true`. The default is `false` (verdict:391-395, :409), and a page that never opts in keeps stage A byte for byte (verdict:57). While a native modal is open, anything outside the modal's own element tree stops responding. That covers a toast in a `.toast-container` on `body`. It also covers a tooltip or popover panel the engine appended to `body`, which is the default placement: Bootstrap's `container: false` resolves to `document.body` (browser-engine-distillate.md:506; veneer:src/browser/Tip.ts:203). The user cannot click the toast's close button, hover the toast to pause autohide, Tab to it, or select its text. Assistive technology does not see it either: the measured accessibility tree excludes every node outside a `showModal()` dialog (sbm:93). A toast message posted outside the modal is therefore not exposed while the modal shows. That last point is inferred from sbm:93, and actual speech is unmeasured (sbm:107). The same holds for any third-party widget that appends its popup to `body`, such as a date picker or an autocomplete list, because the spec makes every node outside the dialog inert (elements:guides/w3c/interactions.md:277). On Bootstrap's path the opposite holds: the toast (z-index 1090, veneer:src/bootstrap/components/_toasts.scss:5) and the tooltip sit over the modal (1055, veneer:src/bootstrap/components/_modal.scss:5) and receive the click first (verdict:521, Bootstrap column). Whether an inert toast stays visible is unmeasured; its pixel compositing is listed as open (sbm:107).
limits.why_native_dialog_causes_it: `showModal()` does three things at once. It puts the dialog in the browser's top layer, it marks the document as blocked by that dialog, and it runs the dialog focusing steps (elements:guides/w3c/elements/interactives.md:669-677). While the document is blocked, every connected node except the dialog and its descendants must become inert (elements:guides/w3c/interactions.md:277). An inert node is hit-tested as if `pointer-events: none` were set, cannot be selected, cannot normally be focused, and is not exposed to assistive technology (interactions.md:265-269). The block follows the topmost dialog in the top layer, not the topmost element. A body-level toast promoted into the top layer and reopened over the modal still lost the hit test to the modal (sbm:105). Elements' own stylesheet records that z-index has no effect on the top layer (elements:src/styles/elements/_dialog.scss:31-32). Veneer's Bootstrap path never calls `showModal()`. It shows a `div.modal` with a separate `div` backdrop, a scripted `Trap`, and a `Lock` (veneer:src/browser/Modal.ts:46-52, :190-210), so nothing outside the modal becomes inert there. The ordinary-layer toast case (not promoted) in `modal-native:order` extends the promoted reading to ordinary-layer toasts by the spec rule. B3 must fill its cells from the implemented branch (verdict:511, :521, :796).
limits.what_elements_did: Elements made native modality the default, so its authors always lived with this limit: `modal` defaults to `true` and calls `showModal()` (elements:src/browser/factories/createDialog.ts:40, :62-63). Its showcase presents inertness as a free benefit: "every element outside the modal is treated as inert ... The framework doesn't have to add this" (elements:app/browser/pages/DialogElementPage.vue:468-470). No factory reacts to an open dialog. The toast, tooltip, and popover factories carry no dialog or modal handling; `createPopover` mentions `dialog` only to exclude it from the anchor surface (elements:src/browser/factories/createPopover.ts:30-36). The toast is promoted into the top layer as a manual popover through `createPopover` (elements:src/browser/factories/createToast.ts:176-204; createPopover.ts:261) and re-appended to its own parent container on every show (createToast.ts:188-191). A toast shown after the dialog therefore paints over it, but it stays inert (sbm:105). Tooltip and popover panels are never moved: the author passes `{ anchor, panel }` and places the panel in markup (elements:src/browser/factories/createTooltip.ts:39-45), so a panel written inside the dialog is a descendant and stays live. The only acknowledgment of the problem is the toast's manual `pause()` and `resume()`, documented for "a sibling modal that should pause the toast" (elements:app/browser/pages/UseToastPage.vue:786-789; createToast.ts:270-287).
limits.what_elements_left_open: Neither the toast factory nor its stylesheet has a rule for a toast under an open modal (addendum:303). No clone test reads hit order or paint between two top-layer surfaces (addendum:229), and the clone has no paint or hit instrument at all (addendum:96-99). The promoted toast takes the float path's ARIA, including `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and an `aria-controls` that names itself (addendum:301). One Escape hides every open float and cancels the modal's own close request (addendum:197). The guides never tell an author that a body-level toast or widget is unusable behind a modal (DialogElementPage.vue:468-470).
limits.veneer_verdict_position: Accept as a documented limit of the opt-in. It appears in the `ModalInterface` remark (verdict:415), the W2 stacking ruling (verdict:796), the `modal-native:order` row (verdict:521), and the guide limits that B7 owns (verdict:883). Toast promotion is refused as scope: promotion does not lift inertness (sbm:105), it takes the toast out of `.toast-container` layout (verdict:196-198), and no consumer asks for it. Recommended: accept (verdict:1184-1190). The 2026-10-06 rulings record no acceptance until you rule on this explanation (user-rulings-2026-10-06.md:9).
limits.author_remedy: For a tooltip or popover, set its `container` to an element inside the modal (verdict:415, :798). The guide already gives this advice for interactive tips inside a focus trap (veneer:guides/veneer.md:595). For a toast, the verdict names no remedy. The nearest measured case is a promoted toast inside the modal's subtree, which hit-tested first (sbm:105). A plain `.toast-container` placed inside the native host is unmeasured. An author whose page must keep body-level toasts or widgets usable during a modal keeps `native` off for that modal.
limits.options_for_user: Option 1, accept (the verdict's recommendation). Cost: authors who opt in place any toast, tip, or widget they need during the modal inside the modal. Body-level toasts stay unusable while the modal is open, and possibly visible (unmeasured). The guide must say so (verdict:883). Pages that do not opt in pay nothing (verdict:57). Option 2, elements' approach: promote toasts and tips into the top layer (createToast.ts:176-204; createTooltip.ts:230). Cost: this repairs paint order only, and the surfaces stay inert (sbm:105; chk:42). Toast promotion replaces container layout with per-frame script layout (addendum:303), and tips already have the gated paint-only `topmost` leaf in B5 (verdict:173, :799). Option 3, a different route: the engine moves body-level toasts and tips into the open host. Cost: refused for tips because it changes a node's parent based on runtime state (verdict:171). It would also move author toast containers and break CSS that targets them by parent. Option 4: keep `native` off. Cost: none of the native gains (the top layer, browser modality, outside exclusion from the accessibility tree at sbm:93, routed `command` and `requestClose()` requests at verdict:150-156). Recommendation: option 1, adding a B3 reading of an ordinary toast-container inside the host before the guide offers it as a toast remedy.

limits.limit: (b) An ordinary-layer tip outside the host paints beneath the modal's content, so a tooltip with Bootstrap's default body container is hidden there until the author sets `container` inside the modal.
limits.plain_meaning: Take a tooltip whose trigger button sits inside an open native modal. With Bootstrap's default container, the engine appends the tooltip to `body` (veneer:src/browser/Tip.ts:203; browser-engine-distillate.md:506). The modal's content box then draws over the tooltip. Where the tooltip overlaps the white `.modal-content` box, the user does not see it, and a popover with links or buttons cannot be clicked anywhere, because of limit (a). On Bootstrap's `div.modal` path, the same tooltip paints over the content (verdict:169; chk:42). The failure makes no sound: no error is raised, and the tip is reported shown.
limits.why_native_dialog_causes_it: The browser paints the top layer over the page's whole normal stacking order, whatever the z-index. The tooltip on `body` stays in the normal order with z-index 1080. The native host and its `.modal-content` are in the top layer, so the content covers the tooltip. The check measured this with known colors. The tooltip pixel read green over an ordinary host. Under a native modal it read the content's red. A manually promoted tooltip read green again, and both native-modal outside tips failed the hit test (chk:190, :42). Promotion therefore fixes paint and leaves inertness, because inertness and paint are separate facts (chk:80).
limits.what_elements_did: Elements never meets the paint half of this limit, because every float it makes is already in the top layer. Its tooltip and popover set `popover="manual"` and open with `showPopover({ source })` (elements:src/browser/factories/createTooltip.ts:28, :230; elements:src/browser/factories/createPopover.ts:197, :261). A tip opened while the dialog is up joins the top layer after the dialog and paints over it by insertion order. Elements has no `container` concept. The author places the panel in markup (createTooltip.ts:39-45), so a panel written inside the dialog is both painted and live. Elements' own records keep its z-index tokens only for surfaces outside the top layer (elements:src/styles/_tokens.scss:227-233; elements:src/browser/tokens.ts:135-138).
limits.what_elements_left_open: No elements test or page reads paint or hit testing for a tip over a dialog (addendum:86, :222, :229), and the dialog playground has no tooltip, popover, or toast case (elements:app/browser/playgrounds/DialogPlaygroundPage.vue, no match). A tip opened before the dialog sits under it in insertion order. That is inferred, and elements has no case for it. No float factory notices a native hide or rolls back a refused promotion (addendum:189-192). One Escape hides every float and swallows a modal's close request (addendum:197). The tooltip writes no `aria-describedby` (addendum:201). A promoted float that keeps `position: absolute` resolves against the initial containing block (addendum:220).
limits.veneer_verdict_position: Ruling 7 states a guide limit, with no reparenting and no throw (verdict:168-173). The limit sits in the `native` TSDoc and in `### Opt into native surfaces` (verdict:170, :415). The `modal-native:paint` row records it (verdict:522). An automatic container is refused because it changes the tip's parent based on runtime state (verdict:171). A `TIP_CONTAINER` throw is refused because it would raise an error on every hover (verdict:172). B5 must confirm whether `topmost` can be offered as a paint-only remedy for tips that hold no controls (verdict:173, :799). Recommended: accept (verdict:1190).
limits.author_remedy: Set the tip's `container` to an element inside the modal. This works under stage A and under the native path (verdict:798), and the guide already asks for it for interactive tips (veneer:guides/veneer.md:595). If B5's reading passes, `topmost` becomes a second remedy, for paint only (verdict:173).
limits.options_for_user: Option 1, accept with the `container` remedy (recommended). Cost: every tip whose trigger sits in a native modal needs `container` set. A data-API tip left at the default fails without any signal: it reports shown and is covered. Option 2, elements' approach: promote the tip into the top layer (`topmost`). Cost: it fixes paint only, so an interactive popover stays dead (chk:42). It is gated on B5's integrated reading (verdict:171-173), and a tip opened before the modal would still sit under it. Option 3: the engine resolves the container to the open dialog automatically. Cost: refused, because the tip's parent then depends on runtime state, and author CSS scoped by parent breaks (verdict:171). Option 4: throw `TIP_CONTAINER`. Cost: refused, because it turns a documented limit into an error on every hover, and the Tip family would test a condition that only the Modal leaf creates (verdict:172).

limits.limit: (c) In a document inside a frame, Tab from the last control leaves the document.
limits.plain_meaning: This limit applies when your page runs inside an iframe, such as an embed, a preview pane, or the Vitest browser runner. With a native modal open, pressing Tab on the modal's last control moves focus out of the iframe into the parent page. Focus does not return to the modal's first control, so a keyboard user ends up outside the dialog and must Shift+Tab back in. In the same framed document on Bootstrap's path, Tab wraps to the first control (chk:82, :185). In a top-level page the behavior is unmeasured (verdict:812; feas:35), so the limit is stated for framed documents only.
limits.why_native_dialog_causes_it: The show-a-modal-dialog steps make everything outside the dialog inert and run the dialog focusing steps. They contain no step that cycles Tab (elements:guides/w3c/elements/interactives.md:673-677, :761-769; addendum:242). With every outside control inert, sequential navigation finds no later focusable element in the document after the last control, so focus leaves the document for the frame's parent. Veneer's `Trap` redirects focus only from a `focusin` event inside its own document (veneer:src/browser/Trap.ts:50-58, :75-85). On Bootstrap's path, Tab first lands on an outside control in the same document, `focusin` fires, and `Trap` sends focus to the first control. That matches Bootstrap's own focustrap, which listens for `focusin` and the Tab key direction (browser-engine-distillate.md:390). Under native, no outside control can take focus, so no `focusin` fires in the child document. This mechanism is inferred from the code. The outcomes are measured (chk:185). The feasibility run saw the same with `inert` alone: Tab left the test iframe, while Bootstrap's FocusTrap cycled (feas:23).
limits.what_elements_did: Elements relied on the browser and claimed the browser traps Tab inside a modal dialog. The claim appears in the factory header (elements:src/browser/factories/createDialog.ts:20-22), the Vue adapter (elements:src/browser/composables/useDialog.ts:11-14), and both showcase pages (elements:app/browser/pages/DialogElementPage.vue:463; elements:app/browser/pages/UseDialogPage.vue:6-8, :216). The dialog factory imports no focus code (createDialog.ts:1-13). Elements does have a separate keydown trap, `createFocus`, which cancels Tab at the last focusable descendant and focuses the first, and the reverse for Shift+Tab (elements:src/browser/factories/createFocus.ts:49-64). It tells authors to use that trap only outside `<dialog>` (elements:src/browser/composables/useFocus.ts:10-13).
limits.what_elements_left_open: The browser Tab-trap claim has no support in the spec card the clone itself carries (addendum:34, correction 3). No elements test presses Tab or reads focus. The dialog suite covers the host gate, show, hide, the veto, event names, the non-modal lock, synthetic `cancel` and `close`, and disposal (elements:tests/src/browser/factories/createDialog.test.ts:21-133, :236-338), and the composable suite covers only show, hide, and toggle (elements:tests/src/browser/composables/useDialog.test.ts:14-45). `createFocus` has no `focusin` guard, so focus that a click or a script moves outside the container stays outside (addendum:162).
limits.veneer_verdict_position: `Trap` stays the sole focus wrapper, because `inert` excludes outside controls without wrapping focus (verdict:312, :784, :810). The `modal-native:tab` row records "outside the document" (verdict:519). The guide states the limit for framed documents only, and the top-level case stays unmeasured (verdict:812, :415). The addendum holds the verdict against elements' trap claim (addendum:59) and gives B7 a spec step to cite (addendum:242). Recommended: accept (verdict:1190).
limits.author_remedy: The verdict names no author remedy. It states the limit. An author whose page runs inside a frame and needs Tab wrapping keeps `native` off for that modal.
limits.options_for_user: Option 1, accept and document it for framed documents (recommended). Cost: framed embeds lose Tab wrapping under the leaf. The top-level case stays unknown until someone measures it, and a reading in a top-level document would settle whether the limit is frame-only. Option 2, elements' approach: rely on the browser. Cost: it is no fix, it gives the same limit, and elements' claim shows how easily the gap goes undocumented. Option 3, a different route borrowed from elements' `createFocus`: give `Trap` a keydown wrap that cancels Tab at the last focusable control under the native path (createFocus.ts:49-64). Cost: it changes the shared `Trap` that the stage A modal and offcanvas use (veneer:src/browser/Modal.ts:51), unless it is gated to the native path. It departs from Bootstrap's focusin design. It must compute the first and last controls with the same visibility and enabled rules `findFocusable` uses (veneer:src/browser/Trap.ts:82). It must not capture Tab while focus sits in a tip inside the modal. It needs readings in both framed and top-level documents before it lands. Option 4: keep `native` off in framed contexts. Cost: the author loses the native gains on those pages.

limits.limit: (d) With `focus: false`, outside focus is still refused.
limits.plain_meaning: Bootstrap's `focus: false` (`data-bs-focus="false"`) lets the user click or Tab to things outside an open modal. Pages use it so that a third-party widget appended to `body`, such as a date picker, an editor menu, or a chat panel, stays usable. Veneer's own TSDoc promises that with `false`, "focus moves freely" (veneer:src/browser/types.ts:1363-1367). Under `native`, that setting only turns off Veneer's trap. The browser still makes the rest of the page unfocusable and unclickable, so on a native modal the setting no longer does what it says. Markup can carry `data-bs-focus="false"`, but markup never sets a leaf (verdict:69). A page that turns on `createModalPlugin({ native: true })` therefore hits this limit on any data-API modal that carries that attribute (verdict:409).
limits.why_native_dialog_causes_it: In Veneer, `focus: false` only skips `this.#trap.activate()` (veneer:src/browser/Modal.ts:208), as in Bootstrap, where a truthy `focus` activates the focustrap (browser-engine-distillate.md:355). Under native, `showModal()` itself makes the outside inert (elements:guides/w3c/interactions.md:277), and no option the engine passes switches that off. The engine also never writes `inert` itself (verdict:784). This is measured: the outside opener could not receive focus while the dialog was modal (feas:13), and outside nodes left the accessibility tree (sbm:93). The `modal-native:focus-off` row records "refused" (verdict:520), and the verdict states it as a row (verdict:811).
limits.what_elements_did: Elements has no `focus` option at all (elements:src/browser/types.ts:1441-1454). Its only way to keep the rest of the page usable is the `modal: false` mode, which calls `show()` instead of `showModal()` (elements:src/browser/factories/createDialog.ts:40, :62-70). That mode gives no top layer, no `::backdrop`, no inertness, and no browser focus handling. The dialog renders inline at its source position (elements:src/styles/elements/_dialog.scss:16-23, :208-212; elements:app/browser/pages/DialogElementPage.vue:474). An opt-in body scroll lock is available (createDialog.ts:66-69; types.ts:1449-1452). Elements turned the outside-focus question into a choice of mode, not a focus switch.
limits.what_elements_left_open: Under `show()`, the `closedby` Auto state computes to None. Escape then fires no `cancel`, so the `dismiss.escape` policy has nothing to act on (addendum:36, correction 5; addendum:257). Elements' own stylesheet records a known jump: a closing non-modal dialog snaps to the viewport center for the close transition (_dialog.scss:195-206). The non-modal lock pads `body` on top of a declared stable gutter (addendum:164). `dismiss.escape: false` also blocks `requestClose()` and the `request-close` command (addendum:137-142).
limits.veneer_verdict_position: The verdict records the departure and asks you to accept it (verdict:520, :811, :1188). It adds no remedy beyond the opt-in nature of the leaf (verdict:1190). The `Trap` still activates at `shown` when `focus` is not `false` (verdict:477).
limits.author_remedy: The verdict names none. An author whose modal must leave outside controls reachable keeps `native` off for that modal, either with a per-modal `ModalOptions.native` or by not using the native plugin option. That is inferred from verdict:391-395 and :409.
limits.options_for_user: Option 1, accept and document it (recommended). Cost: the combination of `focus: false` and `native: true` silently keeps outside focus refused, and the `focus` TSDoc and the guide must say so under the leaf. Option 2, elements' approach: under `native`, open a `focus: false` modal with `show()` (non-modal) instead. Cost: it loses the top layer, browser modality, outside exclusion from the accessibility tree, and the `cancel` route. It adds a third host path to test. It departs from Bootstrap, where `focus: false` keeps the backdrop and modal styling. It also changes `:modal`, which B1's readers and the stylesheet fence observe. Option 3: refuse the combination with a throw. Cost: `data-bs-focus="false"` arrives from markup that the page author may not own, so a native plugin would throw on existing data-API modals. Option 4: the plugin quietly skips `native` for hosts with `focus: false`. Cost: a hidden behavior switch that the opt-in rule's one-leaf shape does not allow (verdict:62-71).

elements_dialog_design: The elements clone at 3b41900 handles dialogs with one factory, `createDialog(element, options)`. It binds only a `<dialog>` host and throws on any other tag (elements:src/browser/factories/createDialog.ts:31-35). `modal` defaults to `true` and calls `showModal()`; `false` calls `show()` (createDialog.ts:40, :62-70). The factory writes nothing on the host: no `inert`, no `closedby`, no `aria-modal`, and no `role` (addendum:416). It leaves the top layer, initial focus, outside inertness, and the backdrop to the browser. It also claims a browser Tab trap and a browser scroll lock that neither the spec nor the records support (createDialog.ts:20-24; addendum:33-34). `show()` dispatches a cancelable `elements:dialog:show`, sets `visible`, calls the native method, and emits `open` after `runTransition`, which waits for `transitionend` or a 400 ms fallback (createDialog.ts:55-77; addendum:419). There are three close routes. First, `hide()` dispatches a cancelable `hide`, calls `close()` at once, and emits `close` after the transition (createDialog.ts:79-100). The CSS exit plays because `display` and `overlay` transition with `allow-discrete` (elements:src/styles/elements/_dialog.scss:140-153). Second, Escape, `method="dialog"` forms, and inner `close()` calls close natively with no veto. `cancel` is cancelled only when `dismiss.escape` is `false`, and the queued `close` event flips `visible` and emits `close` (createDialog.ts:109-129; addendum:126-129). Third, a click whose target is the dialog and whose point falls outside the dialog's rectangle counts as a backdrop click (createDialog.ts:145-157). The scrim is the native `::backdrop`, with no backdrop element. `dialog:modal::backdrop` gets 50% black and a 2px blur, and the transition list sits on the bare `dialog::backdrop`, so the fade-out survives `:modal` dropping at `close()` (elements:src/styles/surfaces/_backdrop.scss:66-67, :90-98, :116-120). Centering sits on ungated `dialog` for the same reason (_dialog.scss:156-186). For the rest of the page, elements relies on browser inertness under `showModal()` and presents it as a free benefit (elements:app/browser/pages/DialogElementPage.vue:468-470). It adds a body scroll lock only for a non-modal dialog with `scroll.lock` (createDialog.ts:66-69). It keeps Bootstrap's z-index scale only for surfaces outside the top layer (elements:src/styles/_tokens.scss:227-246). Nothing in the clone handles toasts, tips, or third-party widgets while a dialog is open. `destroy()` closes an open host without an event (createDialog.ts:166-185), and the Vue `useDialog` builds the factory in a post-flush watch and destroys it on cleanup (elements:src/browser/composables/useDialog.ts:18-50). Its tests run on fake timers and use synthetic `cancel` and `close` events. They have no focus, Tab, paint, or hit case (elements:tests/src/browser/factories/createDialog.test.ts:14-19, :96-122, :204-212).
elements_lessons: Adopted with a change: gate the native path on a real `<dialog>` host. Elements throws on any other tag (elements:src/browser/factories/createDialog.ts:35). Veneer runs native only when `isBrowserDialog(host)` holds and keeps Bootstrap's path otherwise, with no throw (verdict:391, :436, :456-457).

Adopted and extended: a cancelable before-event ahead of the native call. Elements dispatches `show` and `hide` before `showModal()` and `close()` (createDialog.ts:56-57, :80-81). Veneer keeps the `show.bs.modal` and `hide.bs.modal` vetoes. It also routes the native paths elements left ungated through them: commands, script `showModal()`, and `requestClose()` (verdict:150-156, :483-491; addendum:109-113, :126-129).

Adopted: the forced-close model from elements' aside, which emits a non-cancelable `hide` at the synchronous closing `beforetoggle` (elements:src/browser/factories/createAside.ts:81-90; addendum:189-190). Veneer dispatches `hide.bs.modal` with `cancelable: false` there (verdict:157-162, :492-496).

Adopted: the statechart observables `open` and `:modal` from elements' dialog table (elements:tests/src/browser/factories/createDialog.test.ts:217-234; addendum:82-85). They become the `$::open` and `$::modal` departure rows (verdict:515-517).

Adopted with a change: floats enter the top layer only as `popover="manual"`, as elements' popover and tooltip do (elements:src/browser/factories/createPopover.ts:261; createTooltip.ts:230). Veneer refuses `auto` and `hint` (verdict:101, :104). Unlike elements, it writes `popover` only while the panel is open (addendum:63).

Adopted as evidence: rules gated on `:modal` or `[open]` revert at `close()` while the exit tail still renders. Elements therefore moved centering onto bare `dialog` and the backdrop transition onto bare `::backdrop` (elements:src/styles/elements/_dialog.scss:156-186; elements:src/styles/surfaces/_backdrop.scss:90-98). The verdict refuses the `dialog.modal:modal` fence selector for the same reason (verdict:551; addendum:330).

Refused: relying on the browser for a Tab trap. Elements attaches no trap to its dialog and claims one (createDialog.ts:1-13, :20-22). The spec has no Tab-cycling step (addendum:34, :242). `Trap` stays the sole wrapper, and the framed-document limit is stated (verdict:784, :810-812; addendum:59).

Refused: relying on `showModal()` for a scroll lock. Elements ships no modal lock and claims a native one (createDialog.ts:22-24, :60-61). The records measured the page scrolling under a modal (addendum:33, :58; sbm:72). `Lock` stays the sole owner, and `:has(dialog:modal)` locks are refused (verdict:314, :814-815).

Refused: `::backdrop` as the scrim. Elements paints its one scrim on `dialog:modal::backdrop` (elements:src/styles/surfaces/_backdrop.scss:116-120). Veneer keeps Bootstrap's `div` backdrop, which is a transcript node, and makes the native backdrop transparent (verdict:108, :310, :543-545).

Refused: Escape through the native `cancel` event. Elements' `dismiss.escape: false` cancels every `cancel`, which also blocks `requestClose()` and `command="request-close"` (createDialog.ts:109-115; addendum:137-142). Veneer holds `closedby="none"` while the modal shows and keeps Escape on keydown (verdict:306-307, :499).

Refused: reacting to the queued `close` event. Elements' `onNativeClose` can run after a reopen and close the state of an open dialog (createDialog.ts:120-129; addendum:135). Veneer routes no queued `close` or `toggle` event (verdict:159, :462).

Refused: a click-only backdrop route with a rectangle test. Elements dismisses on a press inside the content and a release outside it (createDialog.ts:145-157; addendum:148). Veneer keeps mousedown plus click on the full-viewport host (verdict:500).
Refused: adopting a host that is already open in markup. Elements seeds `visible` from `element.open` (createDialog.ts:43; addendum:75). Veneer throws `MODAL_OPEN` (verdict:416, :465, :497).

Refused: synthetic native lifecycle events in tests, and fake timers. Elements' `nativeclose` row dispatches a fake `close` that leaves `open` and `:modal` true (createDialog.test.ts:204-212, :256-271), and its suites run on `vi.useFakeTimers()` (createDialog.test.ts:14-19). The B1 and B3 rows call the real `close()` and `requestClose()` (addendum:60, :88-91; scaffold AGENTS.md:42).

Refused as scope: toast promotion through the float path. Elements' toast is a manual popover that carries float ARIA and script layout (elements:src/browser/factories/createToast.ts:176-204; addendum:301-303). Ruling 12 refuses toast promotion because inertness survives it (verdict:196-198; sbm:105).

Not taken up: elements answers outside focus with a separate non-modal mode (`modal: false` calls `show()`, createDialog.ts:40, :62-70) instead of a focus switch. The verdict keeps Bootstrap's `focus` key and records that under `native` it no longer frees outside focus (verdict:520, :811).
Confirmation: `closedby="any"` cannot dismiss a full-viewport host. This is a second reason, beside cancelability, for refusing `any` (addendum:143-147; verdict:307).
Confirmation: opening a dialog closes `auto` and `hint` popovers and leaves `manual` ones open, so Veneer's manual floats survive a native modal opening (addendum:154).
Open in no record yet: `returnValue` persists across closes, and a forced close carries no reason. B7 can list it among the limits (addendum:156-159).
